edges.description: Dermal xanthomatized macrophage accumulation produces the papular lesion morphology described clinically.
Xanthomatized macrophage infiltration in papular xanthoma is associated with xanthomatous lesions on the eyelids or periocular region.
edges.target: Yellow xanthomatous eyelid or periocular lesions

edges.description: The pathophysiologic macrophage accumulation is directly observed as the foamy or xanthomatized dermal infiltrate on biopsy.
Xanthomatous macrophage-rich lesions are histologically accompanied by Touton-type giant cells in the clinicopathologic series.

evidence.reference_title: Papular xanthoma: a clinicopathological study of 10 cases.
evidence.snippet: Histology showed moderately well circumscribed exoendophytic papules with a regular epidermis and a dense infiltration of xanthomatized macrophages interspersed by numerous Touton type giant cells.

nodes.description: Papular xanthoma presents as cutaneous papules, usually solitary in the adult clinicopathologic series but also reported as multiple facial papules in childhood.

evidence.reference_title: Papular xanthoma: a clinicopathological study of 10 cases.
evidence.snippet: In this clinicopathologic study, papular xanthoma presented clinically mainly as solitary papule, with a male to female ratio of4 : 1, in an age range from 13 to 57 years and a biphasic occurrence: in the young adolescence and middle ages.

evidence.reference_title: Case report--papular xanthoma in a 10-year-old female with abnormal lipid profile.
evidence.snippet: We report a 10-year-old girl with multiple papule xanthomas on her face that had an abnormal lipid profile.

nodes.description: Papular xanthoma lesions represent a monomorphous non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis reaction pattern dominated by xanthomatized macrophages in skin. Foamy macrophage accumulation and Touton giant cells produce the yellow papular clinical morphology and anchor the diagnosis histologically.

evidence.reference_title: Papular xanthoma: a clinicopathological study of 10 cases.
evidence.snippet: PX represents a monomorphous reaction pattern of n-LCH characterized by the presence of predominantly xanthomatized macrophages.

nodes.description: Xanthomatous lesions can involve eyelid or periocular skin and must be distinguished from xanthelasma and other histiocytoses.

evidence.reference_title: The clinical spectrum of xanthomatous lesions of the eyelids.
evidence.snippet: On the other hand, different types of normolipemic disorders may also cause xanthomatous eyelid lesions. Among these, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, diffuse normolipemic xanthoma, and non-Langerhans cell histiocytoses (papular xanthoma, juvenile xanthogranuloma, xanthoma disseminatum, adult-onset xanthogranuloma, adult-onset asthma and periocular xanthogranuloma, necrobiotic xanthogranuloma, Erdheim-Chester disease, Rosai-Dorfman disease, and reticulohistiocytosis) can be listed.
Histiocytosis is rare but does occur in prevalent locations.
